why: The only code link the paper gives (https://github.com/oyenigun/RouteOptimization) returns 404, so there is no author code and no author dataset to run. The target C1 is nonetheless cheap and fully specified in the text: K-means (k=5, 10 iterations) on 100 Istanbul charging-station points, a GA over the order of the 5 clusters (mutation 0.10, 100 iterations), and a TSP-style ordering inside each cluster, compared against the sequential dataset-order tour (C2). Everything must be reimplemented from the paper's description, and the 100 station coordinates plus the pairwise distance/duration matrix have to be reconstructed since they were shipped only through the dead repository.
missing_artifacts: Author code repository (https://github.com/oyenigun/RouteOptimization returns 'Repository not found')
Istanbul EV charging station dataset: the 100 station records (id, name, latitude, longitude) and their dataset order, which defines both the sequential baseline C2/C4 and the K-means input

Precomputed 100x100 distance (km) and duration (min) matrices used for Table 4; the paper's numbers imply road-network distances (likely Google Maps Directions API), which cannot be regenerated without an API key and are not bit-reproducible in any case

K-means initialization / random seed and GA seed, selection and crossover operators, and the intra-cluster routing rule (exact TSP vs nearest neighbour vs 2-opt) - none are specified precisely enough to pin the exact 308.49 km
blockers_seen: GitHub repository 404: no code, no weights, no data of any kind released
Target dataset is distributed only via that missing repository, so the 100-station coordinates and their ordering must be re-sourced or reconstructed

Reported distances/durations appear to come from a proprietary routing API (Google Maps), so exact reproduction of 308.49 km / 568.15 min is not achievable even with the code; only the qualitative and approximate-magnitude result (large saving over the sequential route) is recoverable

K-means and GA hyperparameters beyond (k=5, 10 iter, mutation 0.10, 100 iter) - selection, crossover, population size, seed, intra-cluster solver - are not reported, so the optimizer's exact output is seed-dependent
No GPU on this machine, but the workload is tiny and CPU-only anyway

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: Under 5 minutes of command time per full run: K-means on 100 points is milliseconds, a 100-iteration GA over 5 cluster centres with a 100x100 distance lookup is a fraction of a second, and the intra-cluster TSP over 5 clusters of ~20 nodes each is trivial with 2-opt. The whole configuration sweep plus baselines is well under a minute; the real cost is writing the ~200 lines of reimplementation.
feasibility.scale_down_plan: Not a runtime scale-down but a fidelity scale-down: rebuild a 100-station Istanbul EV charging-station set from public coordinate sources (or, failing that, sample 100 points from Istanbul's road network weighted toward the published station distribution) and use haversine (or an OSM road-network shortest path) instead of the unrecoverable Google Maps matrix. Keep the full protocol - 100 stations, 5 clusters, 10 K-means iterations, GA mutation 0.10, 100 GA iterations - and average over ~10 random seeds so the K-means/GA seed sensitivity is visible. Expected effect: the absolute value will not land on 308.49 km; what should reproduce is the structure of the result - the optimized tour is far shorter than the 417.53 km sequential tour, of the order of the claimed ~25-35% saving. Ceiling is therefore partially_reproduced.

compute.basis: K-means on 100 points plus a 100-iteration GA over 5 cluster labels with lookup-table distances is sub-second per run, so the estimate is dominated by sourcing/reconstructing the 100 station coordinates and the pairwise matrix rather than by any actual computation.
